<thought>All measured resistances are consistent with a simple series chain from node A to node B passing through the intermediate nodes in the order A → N_a1 → N_a2 → N_a3 → X1 → N_b1 → N_b2 → X2 → N_c1 → N_c2 → B. The resistance between any two nodes equals the sum of the series resistors between them, matching every given measurement. The resistor values are the differences between successive A‑to‑node resistances:

- R1 = 5 Ω (A‑N_a1)
- R2 = 10 Ω (N_a1‑N_a2)
- R3 = 15 Ω (N_a2‑N_a3)
- R4 = 20 Ω (N_a3‑X1)
- R5 = 10 Ω (X1‑N_b1)
- R6 = 15 Ω (N_b1‑N_b2)
- R7 = 20 Ω (N_b2‑X2)
- R8 = 10 Ω (X2‑N_c1)
- R9 = 15 Ω (N_c1‑N_c2)
- R10 = 20 Ω (N_c2‑B)

These values reproduce the total A‑B resistance of 140 Ω and all pairwise measurements.
